query: Which material can be used for enhanced catalytic activity and durability toward HER and HOR, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Iridium oxide (IrO2) nanoparticles can be used for enhanced catalytic activity and durability toward the Hydrogen Evolution Reaction (HER) and Hydrogen Oxidation Reaction (HOR) due to their high surface area, conductivity, and ability to form a stable and active oxide layer.
generation.material_initial_state: Iridium oxide (IrO2) nanoparticles with a diameter of 5-10 nm
generation.intervention: Electrodeposition of IrO2 nanoparticles onto a conductive substrate
generation.conditions: Acidic electrolyte (pH 1-3), temperature range of 20-50°C, and potential range of -0.5 to 1.5 V vs. RHE
generation.structural_mediator: High surface area and conductivity of IrO2 nanoparticles
generation.mechanism: The high surface area and conductivity of IrO2 nanoparticles facilitate the adsorption and desorption of hydrogen atoms, while the stable oxide layer enhances the durability of the catalyst
generation.predicted_outcome: Enhanced catalytic activity with a current density of 10-20 mA/cm² at an overpotential of 0.1-0.3 V, and improved durability with a retention of 80-90% of initial activity after 100 hours of operation
generation.uncertainty: The actual performance of IrO2 nanoparticles may vary depending on the specific synthesis method, electrode substrate, and operating conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Electrochemical measurements of HER and HOR activity using a rotating disk electrode
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the current density at an overpotential of 0.2 V is less than 5 mA/cm², or if the retention of initial activity after 100 hours is less than 50%, the hypothesis is falsified
